name: sedan_8at
source: Plausible 8-speed planetary torque-converter automatic for a 2.0-3.0 L passenger car, NOT a specific gearbox [AS]. Ratios patterned after the published spread of current 8-speed planetary automatics (1st ~4.7, 6th 1.00 direct, 8th ~0.67, spread ~7; Naunheimer et al., Automotive Transmissions, 2nd ed., Springer 2011, ch. 6 - verify before citing). Efficiencies 0.95-0.975 per gear [AS] (planetary sets plus pump drag; direct drive best). Shift clutches: input-referred kinetic capacity 400 N*m, about twice the sedan engine's 200 N*m peak [AS]; torque phase 0.15 s and inertia-phase bound 0.6 s [AS] (a passenger automatic shifts in roughly 0.2-0.5 s). Converter [AS]: K-factor 179 rpm/sqrt(N*m) at stall (K_SI = K_imperial / 1.1644; stall ~2400 rpm against a ~180 N*m engine), rising towards the coupling point; torque ratio 2.0 at stall falling to 1.0 at the coupling point SR 0.85 (typical 1.8-2.4 stall ratio). Pump 0.08, turbine 0.03 kg*m^2 [AS]. Lock-up clutch 400 N*m kinetic, engage 0.6 s / release 0.15 s [AS]. Automatic gearbox plan A1.
